# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
- **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
- **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
- **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
- **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)
- **CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV** – Main Street: clicking a tutorial button should not pass through to the cards below (completed)
- Repo file matches: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0-hud-2dp/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN-peek/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (contextual).


---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-30: Planning completed by Map (herdr-downtime worker). Plan approved by producer ("LGTM") with one scope change: staff specialization buffs localized **per business** (Open Question resolved — "Move to per business staff").
- 2026-08-30: Six child work items created (test-first): CG-0MTFO4H1P00210PE (per-business buff scoping unit tests), CG-0MTFO4HGQ008VAQR (applicant flow unit tests), CG-0MTFO4HVS003ESVB (employment/applicant state + buff scoping impl), CG-0MTFO4IBI005C3GC (applicant trigger engine impl), CG-0MTFO4IQO005673N (walk-on presentation impl), CG-0MTFO4J6U003EBO1 (browser test + docs). Dependencies added (tests before impl; UI depends on state; browser test depends on both impl features).
- 2026-08-30: Description updated: ACs reworded as bullets, "**Key Files:**" bold section fixed per wl grouping convention.
- Gap analysis found the follow-up epic CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (done, shipped) already implements the skill catalog, game-start randomization, buff computation, buff wiring, staff templates, and salary deduction. AC2 is therefore delivered; remaining scope = trigger, hire/decline/let-go, employment slots, presentation, tests/docs.

# Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Marked for producer review**

## Objective

When the turn ends and the IncomePhase resolves, step through all income card effects one at a time, in a phase-based order and pacing that reads clearly to the player. Starting with base income, each affected business/community-space card shows its income coins "counting out" into a coin grid rendered on the card; then synergy, reputation, event, and upcoming-card contributions either fly coins into that grid or (for negative effects) fly coins out. This replaces the current single-fly-to-HUD collection with a legible, per-contribution breakdown.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When I end my turn I want to *see* where my income came from — how much each business produced on its own, how much came from synergy and reputation, and how much events changed—so the economy feels legible and satisfying."
- **Player (reduced motion)** — "I still want to follow the phases and see the contributed amounts, but without the coin flights."

## Problem statement

End-of-turn income is currently collapsed into a single coin-per-slot that arcs to the HUD counter (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE). The player cannot tell how much came from base income vs synergy vs reputation vs event modifiers, which undermines the "watch your town pay out" moment.

## Desired change

Rework the income-collection presentation into a phase-based, per-card coin-grid animation:

1. **Base income "counts out" of each card** — for each producing business/community-space, the card's base income (rounded to nearest 0.5 after this phase) appears as coins (full coin per whole 0.5; half coin for a remainder) that animate out of the card into a coin **grid rendered on the card**. Coins accumulate on the card across phases.
2. **Synergy coins fly in from the synergy line** — coins from the synergy multiplier fly from the synergy line (shared `synergyLineEndpoints` geometry) into the affected card's grid.
3. **Reputation coins fly in from the HUD** — coins from the reputation multiplier fly from the reputation score HUD into the grid.
4. **Event-card effects** — any event card (active duration effects, e.g. Flu Outbreak 0.8×) that affects income flies coins in (boost) or out (reduction) to/from the affected business cards. Duration effects are indicated via animated text lines (see below); single-turn effects just fly the coins.
5. **Upcoming cards** — upcoming cards that affect income either fly coins in, or fly coins out (from the business to the upcoming card, where they disappear).
6. **Grid-to-HUD collection** — at the end of the income step, the accumulated coins on each card's grid fly to the HUD coins counter (reusing/extending the existing fly-to-HUD + final "+total" pop behaviour).

**Coin grid packing (per user):** start as a 5×3 grid; when space runs out, overlap/shrink the coins to fit 10×3, then 15×3, etc. Exact packing "whatever works well" — 3 rows with columns growing (5/10/15...) and shrinking coin size / overlap as needed.

**Rounding (per user, Q8):** each *phase* rounds its own portion to the nearest 0.5 for the coins shown in the grid. The HUD / credited total still uses the exact fractional value (current behaviour preserved).

**Phasing (per user, Q3):** phase-based — all cards show base alongside, then all cards' synergy, then all cards' reputation, then each event, then upcoming-card effects. Each phase lasts ~2–3 seconds. **Reduced motion keeps the phases (same sequence + pacing) but removes the coin animation** (no flights / count-out tweens); the per-phase rounded values still appear.

**Duration-effect text lines (Upcoming panel):** for event cards with a duration, indicate their effect via an animated text line — on a *new* card the effect text animates in one letter at a time with a grow/shrink animation. Then, for each line (new and pre-existing), coins fly to/from the affected business cards. *(The Upcoming-deck-as-face-down-single-card redesign that frees the panel space is a SEPARATE work item — CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 is unrelated (HUD decimals); the deck redesign has no ID yet and is out of scope here.)* This item assumes the panel already has room for these effect lines; if it does not yet, this item proceeds with the best available placement and the deck redesign is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. End-of-turn income walks through phases in order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming), each ~2–3s, with on-card coin grids that accumulate rounded coins per phase (nearest 0.5 per phase).
2. Base coins "count out" of each producing card into its grid; synergy coins fly in from the synergy line; reputation coins fly in from the reputation HUD; event/upcoming effects fly coins in or out to/from the appropriate cards.
3. Grid packing scales from 5×3 to 10×3 to 15×3 by shrinking/overlapping coins as space requires; overflow is visible, not clipped.
4. At the end, grid coins fly to the HUD coins counter with the existing final "+total" pop and coin-pop SFX (extending CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE); the credited HUD total is unchanged (exact fractional total preserved).
5. Duration-effect events show an animated effect line (one-letter grow/shrink reveal for new cards) with coins flying to/from affected businesses; single-turn events just fly coins.
6. Reduced motion keeps the same phases and pacing but strips coin animations (text/phase progression only); replay/headless modes are unaffected (no rendering/audio — documented exemption).
7. New/extended unit + browser tests cover phase ordering, per-phase rounding, grid packing stress (15×3+), event/upcoming fly-in/out, and reduced-motion path.
8. All related documentation updated (code comments, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, scene README).

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8). Must remain non-blocking like the current animation (runs inside the turn-advance window; failures swallowed).
- Reuse existing helpers: `moveGameObject`, `popTextOrIcon`, `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention), `synergyLineEndpoints`, per-slot data from `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown`.
- Respect reduced-motion (SettingsStore / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop` etc.
- Must build on / not regress CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE (existing fly-to-HUD) and CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation animation).

## Existing state

- `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` returns `IncomeResult.breakdown` (`SlotIncome[]`: `slotIndex`, `businessName`, `baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) + `handSynergyTotal`; applies per-slot `income-multiplier` active effects, then the reputation multiplier to the total (exact fractional coins).
- `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomeCollection()` (from CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE) flies one coin per producing slot + rep pips to HUD, with final pop; `incomeCollectionActive` flag suppresses the immediate HUD delta pop.
- `synergyLineEndpoints()` shared by renderer + animator for synergy-line geometry (p1/p2/mid).
- `ActiveEffect` system (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier`) with `applyActiveEffectMultiplier()`; duration events e.g. Flu Outbreak (0.8×/5 turns), Recession (0.7×/4), Tourist Season (1.15×/3), Labor Shortage (0.9×/3).
- The "Upcoming" panel (`MainStreetRenderer`) shows the incident queue (2 face-up cards + deck) + ⚠ active-effect duration lines.
- HUD geometry mirrors: coins label at `gameW*0.25 + 70`, rep label at strip centre (`gameW*0.5`), `hudY` from layout.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new `animateIncomePhases()` (or rework `animateIncomeCollection`) implementing the phased coin-grid + fly-in/out sequence; grid-packing helper.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — expose/derive per-slot base/synergy/rep/event contribution breakdown for the phases (likely extend `applyIncome`/`IncomeResult` with richer per-phase data).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()` / `applyIncome()` — surface per-phase contributions (base, synergy, rep from `applyReputationMultiplier`, event deltas) for the animation.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `reputationCoinMultiplier()` — source of the rep-coins fly-in amount.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` / `activeEffects` — identify income-affecting event/upcoming cards for fly-in/out.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Upcoming panel effect-line placement; HUD target coords; on-card grid anchoring.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — orchestrate the phased animation in `endTurn()` income presentation.
- `src/core-engine/ActiveEffect.ts` — reference for `income-multiplier` / `applyActiveEffectMultiplier`.
- `tests/main-street/` — phase-ordering, rounding, grid-packing, reduced-motion tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Grid space / readability** — on-card coin grids may visually clutter small card faces; the 5×3→10×3→15×3 overlap/shrink packing may become hard to read at high income. Mitigate: half-coin vs full-coin sizing, controlled overlap, overflow label. (Spike if needed.)
- **Phase timing vs turn pacing** — 2–3s × several phases could lengthen end-of-turn. Reduced-motion retains phases; keep total within acceptable bounds and non-blocking. Player may find 5+ phases too slow — may need a cap/condense for cards with no contributions in a phase.
- **Rounding drift** — per-phase nearest-0.5 rounding means displayed coins may not sum exactly to the exact credited fractional total; the HUD shows the exact total (documented as intended, Q8).
- **Panel space for effect lines** — the Upcoming-deck redesign (face-down single deck) that frees space is a separate work item; if space isn't ready, effect lines may need a temporary placement. Track the deck redesign as a child/related item.
- **Scope creep** — remain a presentation-only income-animation feature; do not include the deck redesign, Community Favour, HUD decimals, or other economy changes. Log extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Related work

- CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — base the phased animation on this.
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR "Synergy link formation animation" (completed) — synergy-line geometry reuse.
- CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B / CG-0MSX2PNSJ000YDM0 "synergyLineEndpoints" — shared synergy geometry helper.
- CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S "Group C: Investment events — new duration types" — duration `income-multiplier`/`rep-multiplier` events (Flu Outbreak, Tourist Season, etc.) that produce the effect lines.
- CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 "Show HUD bar money and reputation to 2 decimal places" (open) — touches HUD numeric display; related but out of scope.
- Upcoming-deck redesign (face-down single card) — separate work item (no ID yet); prerequisite for freeing Upcoming panel space.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map → user): "End state of the coin grid after all coins land?" — Answer (user): "(a) Grid is intermediate — coins then fly from each card to the HUD counter, replacing the current per-slot fly-to-HUD; the grid visualizes the breakdown, then the existing collection animation finishes the job." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (Map → user): "What are 'upcoming cards that affect income'?" — Answer (user): "Not all cards have a duration effect, some are single turn. For duration cards we need an effect indication (space freed by the Upcoming-deck redesign). If a new card, its effect text animates in (one letter at a time, grow/shrink). Then for each line (new + old) coins fly to/from the affected businesses. Single-turn cards simply fly the coins." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (Map → user): "Sequencing/pacing?" — Answer (user): "Phase based; each phase 2–3 seconds. Reduced motion keeps the phases but removes the animations." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (Map → user): "Grid capacity & card space + packing?" — Answer (user): "5×3 grid to start; overlap/shift coins to enable 10×3, then 15×3, etc." Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 (Map → user): "Fractional rounding for portions?" — Answer (user): "Round for the total after each phase." Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (Map → user): "Is the Upcoming-deck redesign part of this item?" — Answer (user): "It is another work item." Source: interactive reply.
- Q7 (Map → user): "Exact 5×3→10×3→15×3 packing rule?" — Answer (user): "Whatever works well." Source: interactive reply.
- Q8 (Map → user): "Round per phase means each phase rounds its own coins to nearest 0.5 independently?" — Answer (user): "confirm." Source: interactive reply.
- Q9 (Map → user): "Base coins stay on the card as grid anchor; at end grid coins fly to HUD?" — Answer (user): "confirm." Source: interactive reply.

## Mini-review record (agent, five stages)

- **1. Completeness:** Problem, users, ACs, constraints present. ACs cover phase ordering/rounding, per-contribution fly-in/out, grid packing stress, event text lines, reduced-motion, tests, docs. Added a grid-overflow visibility AC (never clipped) and a build/doc AC.
- **2. Capture fidelity:** All user answers (Q1–Q9) captured verbatim in the Appendix; phased/pacing/reduced-motion (Q3), 5×3→10×3→15×3 packing + "whatever works well" (Q4/Q7), per-phase total rounding (Q5/Q8), deck redesign out of scope (Q6), base-counts-out + grid-intermediate-then-fly-to-HUD (Q1/Q9). No intent altered.
- **3. Related-work & traceability:** Key precedents linked (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B/CG-0MSX2PNSJ000YDM0, CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S). find-related automated report appended; its hits are mostly tangential (hand animation, Coloretto spacing) and do not alter scope.
- **4. Risks & assumptions:** Added grid-readability, phase-timing/turn-pacing, per-phase rounding drift, Upcoming-panel space (deck redesign out of scope), and a scope-creep guard. Each has a mitigation.
- **5. Polish & handoff:** Tightened objective to "phase-based, per-card coin grid + fly-in/out" with measurable ACs; documented exact credited total preserved (Q8); highlighted which helpers to reuse and the separate deck-redesign work item.

## Related work (automated report)

Automated find-related report appended to this item's description (.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ.md) — hits: CG-0MS7UEUL000610A2 (buy-card hand animation, tangential), CG-0MSJFUGB5005YBK8 (Coloretto tableau spacing, tangential), CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9 (synergy bonus on cards, related). Manual related-work section above lists the truly-direct precedents.

**Research summary:** Reviewed `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown` (per-slot base/synergy, per-slot income-multiplier, then total rep multiplier), `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomeCollection()` and its `incomeCollectionActive` suppression, `synergyLineEndpoints` shared geometry, `ActiveEffect`/`applyActiveEffectMultiplier` for duration events, `reputationCoinMultiplier()` in MainStreetDifficulty (divisor 20, max 3.0), and the Upcoming panel renderer. Related completed items CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MSQJ244M0055X7S guide the design.

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Tutorial Coverage for Action Banking

## Problem statement

The action banking mechanic is fully implemented and visible in the HUD (banked-action counter + tooltip), but the 23-step Main Street tutorial never mentions or teaches it. New players have no guidance on how unused actions accumulate across days, the cap of 2, or how staff-derived actions (e.g., General Manager) are consumed first.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they need to understand that saving actions across days is a strategic option, not wasted turns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Tutorial step teaches banking concept:** At least one tutorial step (confirm or action-gated) explains that unused actions bank up to a cap of 2 and are carried into future days.
- 2. **Tutorial explains staff-first consumption:** Tutorial copy states that staff-derived actions (e.g., General Manager's +1) are spent before base/banked actions and never bank themselves.
- 3. **HUD banked counter highlighted:** A tutorial step highlights the banked-action count in the HUD action counter (e.g., "2 actions left (1 banked)") so players learn where to check their reserve.
- 4. **i18n keys added:** New tutorial text keys registered in `tutorial-en.ts` following the `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern.
- 5. **No regressions:** Existing 23-step tutorial flow, copy, and gate logic remain unchanged; all existing tests pass.

## Constraints

- **Tutorial-only changes:** No core-engine, card-system, rule-engine, or UI component changes. Only tutorial copy and step definitions.
- **Editorial rules apply:** ≤3 sentences per text box, exactly one point per box; no time-limited play mentions; no hardcoding of card names/costs in step strings that could go stale.
- **Minimal integration:** Prefer inserting banking into an existing step (e.g., T6 — first End Turn) rather than adding new steps, to keep the tutorial length stable. If a new step is necessary, it must be justified by a clear pedagogical need.
- **Action banking is already implemented:** All engine, state, HUD, and tooltip work from CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR and its children is complete.

## Existing state

- **HUD:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders the action counter as `<remaining> action(s) left` with a `(<banked> banked)` suffix when `bankedActions > 0`.
- **Tooltip:** `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildActionTooltip()` explains banking and appends a GM note when employed.
- **Tutorial:** 23 steps (T1–T23), defined in `TutorialFlow.ts` (`UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`), copy in `tutorial-en.ts`. Step T6 is the first End Turn — a natural place to introduce banking.
- **Editorial rules:** Documented in `tutorial-en.ts` header (≤3 sentences, no hardcoded card facts, two-turn plan-ahead only).

## Desired change

Add 1–2 tutorial steps (or extend an existing step) that teach action banking: the concept (unused actions bank up to 2), the HUD indicator (where to look), and the staff-first rule. All changes are in tutorial copy/step definitions only — no engine or UI refactoring.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Add new tutorial step strings (title/body keys) for banking concept.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Add new step definition(s) to `UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS` or extend an existing step's body text.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Potentially adjust scenario to produce a day with banked actions if the teaching step requires observing them.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — Add a highlight zone for the action counter (if not already covered) to guide the player to the banked count.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialState.ts` — Verify no state changes needed; banking is engine-managed.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (done) — Main Street: action banking (parent feature; banking logic, state, persistence).
- **CG-0MT4ZHQU9003MWER** (done) — HUD banked counter + GM-aware tooltip (AC5 of parent).
- **CG-0MT4ZHR9M007VP9D** (done) — Document action banking in core rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Step count increase:** Adding a banking step increases the tutorial from 23 to 24+ steps. Prefer embedding banking text into an existing step (e.g., T6's body) to avoid length bloat.
- **Scenario alignment:** Teaching banking may require the tutorial scenario to produce a day where the player ends without acting (so banked > 0 on day 2+). If the current scenario always uses the action, the scenario may need a minor tweak.
- **Assumption — no new HUD zones:** The tutorial overlay highlight system already supports `hud` and `actionButtons` zones; if the action counter doesn't have its own zone, a small addition may be needed.

- Q1 (scope): "Does this include new tutorial steps, or just adding banking text to existing steps?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "Both options are viable; prefer embedding into existing steps (T6 — first End Turn) to keep tutorial length stable. A new step is only justified if the concept is too dense to share." Source: self-research of tutorial structure and editorial rules. Accepted: prefer embedding; new steps only if pedagogically necessary.
- Q2 (scenario): "Does the current tutorial scenario produce a day where the player ends without acting (banked > 0)?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "The current scenario (T3 move Laundromat → T6 end turn) banks 0 on day 1 because the move consumes the action. Day 2 (T7 place) uses the action again. Banking is never observed. A teaching step may need a scenario adjustment — either an 'idle day' step, or a rephrased T6 body that explains banking even when banked=0." Source: self-research of TutorialScenario.ts and budget analysis in TutorialFlow.ts. Accepted: the tutorial copy should explain banking regardless of whether banked > 0 on the first pass; the scenario does not need changes unless the teaching demands an idle day (deferred if scope-creep risk).
- Q3 (step placement): "Where should banking be taught — T4 (Your Hand), T6 (End Turn), or a new step?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "T6 (End Turn) is the natural place: 'End the day to collect income and start the next one. Any unused actions bank up to 2 for future days.' This is concise, one-point, ≤3 sentences, and fits the editorial rules." Source: self-research of step content and action economy flow. Accepted: T6 extension preferred.

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Banking-Aware AI Strategy (Deliberate Action Hoarding)

## Problem Statement

Main Street's AI strategies (GreedyStrategy, RandomStrategy) consume the daily action budget greedily every turn with no concept of action banking. Since action banking (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR) lets unused actions persist across days (capped at 2), the AI never conserves actions — it spends everything and loses the remainder. Banking is therefore a human-only strategic tool. The AI needs a deliberate hoarding strategy that banks actions on some days to enable bigger multi-action plays later (e.g., move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, premium placement), with look-ahead depth and aggressiveness that scales down at lower difficulties.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they expect the AI opponent to use the same strategic tools humans have, making games feel strategically deep and fair at each difficulty.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking-aware AI to be testable (unit + Monte Carlo), balanceable by difficulty, and cleanly separated from the existing Greedy strategy.

Example user stories:

- "As a player on Medium/Hard, I want the AI to occasionally skip a low-value spend to bank an action for a high-value play I can see coming, so the opponent feels thoughtful."
- "As a player on Easy, I want the AI to under-bank compared to higher difficulties, so difficulty still matters."
- "As a developer, I want a distinct banking-aware strategy I can select in Monte Carlo and tune per difficulty, without risking regression in the existing Greedy baseline."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New banking-aware strategy (separate from Greedy):** A new `BankingGreedyStrategy` class is added alongside the existing `GreedyStrategy` — Greedy is left unchanged; `RandomStrategy` is unchanged. The new strategy implements `MainStreetAiStrategy` and is selectable by name (e.g. `BankingGreedy` / `banking-greedy`) wherever strategies are chosen.

2. **Deliberate hoarding behaviour:** The new strategy can choose `end-turn` even when `actionsRemaining > 0` when hoarding is higher-value than spending. When the heuristic's expected value of banking exceeds the best immediate spend's value, the AI banks; otherwise it spends normally via the existing Greedy scoring/priority logic.

3. **Hybrid banking heuristic with difficulty-scaled look-ahead (Q1c + Q3 + Q6):** A new scoring function evaluates the value of banking by considering (a) currently visible unaffordable high-value targets — in hand and in the market row — and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline. The heuristic factors current `bankedActions`, the target's cost vs. available coins, and the AI planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon()` from CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W). Look-ahead depth / banking aggressiveness is reduced at lower difficulties (e.g., Easy banks rarely / looks only at visible cards, Hard considers deeper look-ahead and banks more aggressively). The exact tuning is documented in code comments and validated by tests.

4. **Bank-cap handling — natural via heuristic (Q4: producer leaves to implementer):** No special-case "always bank" branch; the heuristic naturally handles the cap — at `bankedActions == 2` the value of further banking is zero/negative, so the AI spends. Spending and cap enforcement already come from the engine (Q4 accepted as implementer's call to let the heuristic govern).

5. **Monte Carlo harness integration as a new strategy variant (Q5: new):** The Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) registers a new strategy name distinct from `greedy` (e.g., `banking-greedy`) so runs can compare baseline Greedy vs. banking-aware. Guardrail tests (`monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` or equivalent) stay green within tolerance for the new strategy (or a drift report + baseline update is produced per policy CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2); existing `greedy`/`random` baselines are not silently replaced.

6. **Tests — deterministic banking scenarios:** Unit tests in `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) cover, deterministically: (a) the new strategy hoards when a visible high-cost target exists that is currently unaffordable, (b) it spends when no valuable future target justifies hoarding, (c) it does not over-hoard (banks toward cap then spends), (d) it respects action-budget limits and existing legality constraints, (e) difficulty scaling — Easy hoards less than Hard given the same state. Existing `ai-action-budget` and `monte-carlo` tests remain green.

7. **Documentation:** `docs/main-street/` (or equivalent) and in-code comments document the new strategy's existence, when it banks vs. spends, and how difficulty scales look-ahead/aggressiveness. No tutorial changes (Q7: no).

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Additive strategy:** `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` are left unchanged; the banking-aware behaviour lives in a new class so existing behaviour can still be baseline-tested.
- **Bank cap 2, at-most-1 banked per day, day-start composition `1 + gmBonus + min(2, banked)` — all unchanged**; spending / capping comes from the engine. Engine correctly decrements banked on action spend (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC).
- **Hybrid heuristic required (Q1c):** consider both immediate visible targets and look-ahead, with look-ahead reduced at lower difficulties (Q1 parenthetical) and overall aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Q6: yes).
- **Banking-aware strategy is a new Monte Carlo strategy name (Q5):** do not replace the existing `greedy` entry.
- **Tutorial unaffected (Q7: no)** — tutorial coverage for action banking remains the separate item CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.
- **Prerequisite:** Bank-consumption fix CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC (in_review) — banking-aware AI builds on its corrected `consumeAction` semantics; track the dependency and adapt if that fix's semantics shift.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `GreedyStrategy` with an 11-step priority chain (play business/upgrade from hand, buy upgrade, buy business, move-to-hand, buy event, play event, discard, community favour, hire staff, end-turn) and horizon-scored business/upgrade valuators. No banking concept. `RandomStrategy` is budget-oblivious uniform pick. Both respect budget only via `enumerateLegalActions` filtering.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `bankedActions: number` field (init 0), serialized/deserialized, included in undo/redo snapshots.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — `executeDayStart` composes `bankedActions` into the day budget; `processEndOfTurn` banks unused actions; engine/command spend paths decrement `bankedActions` (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC, in_review).
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — runs `GreedyStrategy` / `RandomStrategy` across seeds and difficulties (`MonteCarloStrategy = 'market-greedy' | 'demo-greedy' | 'greedy' | 'random'`); guardrail tests compare to `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`.
- `aiPlanningHorizon()` (CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W) — `clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score)/8), 5, 25)` used for scoring business/upgrade income over future turns; available to reuse for banking valuation.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` validates AI respects the action budget; does not test banking-aware decisions.

## Desired Change

Add a new `BankingGreedyStrategy` that wraps/extends the existing Greedy valuation but first evaluates an implicit "bank actions" option: score the best immediate legal spend vs. score the expected value of banking one action given visible + look-ahead targets and difficulty-scaled look-ahead depth. When banking wins, return `end-turn` early (deliberate hoard); otherwise delegate to the standard Greedy priority chain. Register the new strategy under a distinct name in the Monte Carlo harness so `banking-greedy` can be run and guarded separately from `greedy`.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add `BankingGreedyStrategy` (and supporting `scoreBankOption()` / look-ahead helpers); leave `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` unchanged; document difficulty scaling in comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Register new `banking-greedy` strategy name (extend `MonteCarloStrategy` union + `ALL_STRATEGIES`, wire `createAiPlayerForStrategy`); keep existing `greedy` path unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic unit tests for (a) hoard vs. spend, (b) no over-hoard to cap-then-spend, (c) budget legality, (d) difficulty-scaled aggressiveness, (e) hybrid visible + look-ahead triggers.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (or new guardrail file) — Include/validate the new strategy; drift report + baseline update if intentionally shifted, per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy.
- `docs/main-street/` — AI behaviour section documenting the new strategy and difficulty scaling.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed) — Action banking mechanic (state + engine + UI + tests). Prerequisite this builds on.
- **CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC** (in_review) — Bank consumption fix (decrement banked on action via shared `consumeAction`). Prerequisite for correct banking semantics.
- **CG-0MSX41S7I009MMZN** (completed) — AI & Monte Carlo action budget awareness — existing tests validate AI respects budget.
- **CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W** (completed) — AI threshold-distance planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon`) — reused for banking valuation.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — Base action economy (`actionsRemaining`, `actionsPerTurn`).
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (open) — Tutorial coverage for action banking. Explicitly out of scope here per Q7.
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC** (completed) — PRD Milestone 6 extraction/refactoring (automated find_related match).
- **Automated find_related** at intake start also surfaced repo file matches under `example-games/main-street/` and `tests/main-street/` consistent with the Key Files above; full report sidecar at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Monte Carlo baseline drift:** Banking-aware runs may shift win-rate / coin-per-turn. Per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy produce a drift report and re-baseline only when the shift is intentional (not a hidden regression).
- **Look-ahead complexity:** Hybrid visible + deck look-ahead is more complex than visible-only; scope the look-ahead narrowly (few cards ahead / top of deck) and gate depth by difficulty to keep the strategy testable. If look-ahead proves too noisy, narrow to visible targets with a documented fallback.
- **Over-/under-hoarding:** Too aggressive ⇒ AI seems passive; too timid ⇒ no observable banking. Mitigate with difficulty-scaled thresholds and the four deterministic tests in AC6.
- **Dependency on CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC:** If the bank-consumption fix's semantics change before it lands, this strategy's valuation must adapt — track the dependency.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Per-difficulty Strategy parameter objects, hint-system integration, or re-tunable economy rebalancing are out of scope — record as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 — Banking heuristic trigger: "What determines when the AI should bank vs. spend? (a) visible unaffordable high-value targets, (b) look-ahead at market/deck, (c) hybrid?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01, this session): "c (where look ahead is reduced at lower difficulty levela)".** Source: interactive reply this session. Research: inspected `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (Greedy priority chain + `aiPlanningHorizon`), `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` strategy wiring, and `MainStreetState.ts` banked fields (see context-gathering in prior intake). Resolved: hybrid visible + look-ahead, with reduced look-ahead at lower difficulties.
- Q2 — Strategy granularity: "Parameter on GreedyStrategy, new BankingGreedyStrategy, or modify Greedy in place?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: additive new class; Greedy and Random left unchanged.
- Q3 — Hoarding depth: "How far ahead should the AI plan; leverage aiPlanningHorizon?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: reuse `aiPlanningHorizon()` for banking valuation alongside the new heuristic.
- Q4 — Bank cap interaction: "When already at cap (2), still evaluate banking or handle via heuristic?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "your call".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: implementer's call — heuristic naturally returns zero/negative value at cap so the AI spends; no special-case branch (documented in AC4).
- Q5 — Monte Carlo strategy variant: "New banking-greedy name or replace existing greedy?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: distinct `banking-greedy` strategy name; existing `greedy`/`random` unchanged.
- Q6 — Difficulty tuning: "Should banking aggressiveness vary by difficulty?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: aggressiveness / look-ahead depth scales with difficulty (Easy less aggressive than Hard).
- Q7 — Tutorial: "Does tutorial need to cover banking-aware AI?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "no".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: no tutorial changes; tutorial banking remains CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.
